pronouns.title: Pronouns
pronouns.summary: Kokborok personal pronouns distinguish three persons (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and two numbers (singular, plural). Third-person personal pronouns ('bo' / 'bini') are naturally gender-neutral, applying equally to he, she, and it. Demonstratives and interrogative pronouns serve spatial and interrogative functions.

rules.name: Personal Pronoun Inventory
rules.description: 1st person: 'ang' (I), 'chwng' (we); 2nd person: 'nwng' (you sg.), 'norok' (you pl.); 3rd person: 'bo' (he/she/it), 'borok' (they). Notice 'borok' also means human beings or Tripuri people.

rules.name: Gender Neutrality in Third Person
rules.description: Unlike English ('he' vs 'she') or Hindi ('वह' with verb gender agreement), Kokborok 'bo' is completely gender-neutral. The predicate verb never changes for gender.

rules.name: Demonstrative Pronouns
rules.description: Proximate demonstrative: 'abo' or 'o' (this); Distant demonstrative: 'phaye' or 'aro' (that/there). Locative demonstratives: 'oro' (here), 'aro' (there).

rules.name: Interrogative Pronouns
rules.description: Question pronouns: 'sabo' (who?), 'tamo' / 'tammo' (what?), 'bahai' (how?), 'bano' / 'baha' (where?), 'basing' (when?), 'tamobagwi' (why?).

authentic_examples.english: I will go to the village.
authentic_examples.source: Pai (1976), Kokborok Grammar, CIIL; Tripura Primers

source_references: Pai, Pushpa (1976), 'Kokborok Grammar', Central Institute of Indian Languages, pp. 38-42
Hoque, Faijul (2014), 'Kokborok: A Major Tribal Language of Tripura', IOSR-JHSS
Tripura Language Primers, Directorate of Kokborok & OML, Govt. of Tripura

nouns_and_plurals.title: Nouns and Plural Forms
nouns_and_plurals.summary: Kokborok nouns do not inflect for grammatical gender, but sex distinctions for animate beings are indicated with lexical markers (-chla for male, -bwrwi for female). Plurals are marked by the productive suffix '-rog' (or '-rok'). When counting nouns, numeral classifiers (such as 'kai-', 'khorok-', 'ma-') are obligatory.

rules.name: Plural Suffix '-rog'
rules.description: Attached directly to nouns and pronouns to indicate plural number. For example: 'borok' -> 'borokrog' (people), 'tok' -> 'tokrog' (birds), 'nok' -> 'nokrog' (houses), 'baphang' -> 'baphangrog' (trees).

examples.english: The people live in the village.

rules.name: Natural Gender Markers in Nouns
rules.description: Masculine marker: '-chla' or '-la' (e.g., 'bwsla' = son, 'pun-chla' = male goat). Feminine marker: '-bwrwi' or '-sa' (e.g., 'bwswrwi' = daughter, 'pun-bwrwi' = female goat).

rules.name: Obligatory Numeral Classifiers
rules.description: Kokborok requires a classifier prefix before the numeral when counting items. 'kai-' is used for general inanimate things and fruits ('nok kaisa' = one house); 'khorok-' is used for human beings ('borok khoroksa' = one person); 'ma-' is used for animals and birds ('pun masa' = one goat).

verbs_and_patterns.title: Verbs and Verb Patterns
verbs_and_patterns.summary: Kokborok verbs are agglutinative. The bare verb root serves as the base, onto which suffixes for tense, aspect, mood, and negation attach. Verbs do not inflect for grammatical person, number, or gender, simplifying verbal agreement while maintaining expressive aspectual and modal distinctions.

rules.name: Invariable Verb Agreement
rules.description: Verbs do not change endings for 1st, 2nd, or 3rd person. 'Ang phaikha' (I came), 'Nwng phaikha' (You came), 'Bo phaikha' (He/she came) all use the identical verb form 'phaikha'.

rules.name: Imperative Mood Suffix '-di'
rules.description: Expresses a polite request or standard command directed to second person. Root 'phai' (come) -> 'phaidi' (please come); Root 'cha' (eat) -> 'chadi' (please eat); Root 'thang' (go) -> 'thangdi' (please go).

rules.name: Infinitive / Purposive Suffix '-na'
rules.description: Marks the infinitive or purposive verbal form ('to do X', 'in order to X'). Root 'thang' -> 'thangna' (to go); Root 'cha' -> 'chana' (to eat).

examples.english: I want to go to school.

tense_and_aspect.title: Tense and Aspect
tense_and_aspect.summary: Kokborok distinguishes three primary temporal frames: Present/Habitual, Past (completed/perfective), and Future. These are realized through distinct suffixal morphemes and auxiliary verb constructions.

rules.name: Past / Perfective Marker '-kha'
rules.description: Indicates completed actions in the past. Root + '-kha'. Root 'thang' (go) -> 'thangkha' (went / has gone); Root 'phai' (come) -> 'phaikha' (came / has arrived); Root 'cha' (eat) -> 'chakha' (ate).

rules.name: Future Marker '-nai'
rules.description: Indicates an action that will take place in the future. Root + '-nai'. Root 'thang' -> 'thangnai' (will go); Root 'phai' -> 'phainai' (will come); Root 'cha' -> 'chanai' (will eat).

examples.english: I will go to the village.

rules.name: Present Habitual Suffix '-o' and Progressive Aspect
rules.description: Simple present/habitual uses suffix '-o' (e.g., 'chao' = eats, 'phaio' = comes). Continuous/progressive aspect is constructed with the conjunctive participle '-wi' followed by the auxiliary 'tong' (to stay/exist): 'mai chawi tong' (is eating rice).

source_references: Hoque, Faijul (2014), 'Kokborok: A Major Tribal Language of Tripura', IOSR-JHSS

negation.title: Negation
negation.summary: Kokborok negates verbal clauses predominantly through suffixation rather than independent pre-verbal negative particles. The suffix '-ya' attaches directly to the verb stem for present and future negation, while negative existential 'kwrwi' indicates absence.

rules.name: Present/Future Negative Suffix '-ya'
rules.description: Attaches directly to the verb root. Stem + '-ya'. Root 'thang' (go) -> 'thangya' (does not go / will not go); Root 'cha' (eat) -> 'chaya' (does not eat); Root 'phai' (come) -> 'phaiya' (does not come); Root 'man' (can/get) -> 'manya' (cannot).

examples.english: He/she does not come / will not come.

rules.name: Negative Existential 'kwrwi'
rules.description: Means 'there is not / does not exist / absent'. It functions as the direct negative counterpart of the existential verb 'tong' (to be / to exist).

rules.name: Incompleted Past Negative '-yakho'
rules.description: Formed by combining negative '-ya' with aspectual particle '-kho', indicating an action that has not occurred yet ('not yet').

authentic_examples.english: There is no water in the house.

questions.title: Questions
questions.summary: Kokborok employs two primary question-formation strategies: polar (yes/no) questions marked by sentence-final particles, and content (wh-) questions using interrogative pronouns in-situ without requiring syntactic inversion.

rules.name: Polar (Yes/No) Question Particle '-de' / 'ba'
rules.description: Formed by taking a declarative sentence and adding the question particle '-de' (or 'ba') at the end of the clause. Word order remains unchanged.

rules.name: In-Situ Interrogatives
rules.description: Interrogative words ('sabo' = who, 'tamo' = what, 'bahai' = how, 'bano' = where) occupy the natural syntactic slot of the element being questioned (in-situ), without fronting or auxiliary inversion.

examples.english: What is your name? (Literally: Your name what?)
Where will you go? (Literally: You where will_go?)

sentence_structure.title: Sentence Structure and Word Order
sentence_structure.summary: Kokborok is fundamentally a Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) language, typical of the Tibeto-Burman language family. Adjectives generally follow the noun they modify or carry the adjectival prefix 'kw-' / 'k-'. Subordinate clauses precede main clauses.

rules.name: Strict SOV (Subject - Object - Verb) Order
rules.description: The finite verb consistently appears in sentence-final position. The typical linear order is: Subject + Indirect Object + Direct Object + Verb.

examples.english: Father gave me money. (Apa=S, angno=IO, rang=DO, rwikha=V)

rules.name: Noun-Adjective Order (Post-Nominal Modification)
rules.description: Descriptive adjectives typically follow the head noun: Noun + Adjective. For example, 'nok' (house) + 'kwtal' (new) = 'nok kwtal' (a new house); 'khumpui' (flower) + 'kwchak' (red) = 'khumpui kwchak' (red flower).

rules.name: Pre-verbal Adverbial Placement
rules.description: Adverbs of time, manner, and place are placed before the verb, frequently between the subject and object, or at the sentence onset for topicalization.

examples.english: He/she will go to the village today.

authentic_examples.source: Pai (1976), Kokborok Grammar, CIIL, p. 82; Hoque (2014)

authentic_examples.breakdown: Chwng [Subject] nok kwtal [Noun + Adjective Object] nuk-o [Verb]

source_references: Hoque, Faijul (2014), 'Kokborok: A Major Tribal Language of Tripura', IOSR-JHSS

postpositions.title: Postpositions and Case Markers
postpositions.summary: Kokborok is an agglutinative postpositional language. It does not use prepositions (like English 'in', 'to', 'for'). Instead, grammatical relations and spatial roles are marked by case suffixes and postpositional words directly following the noun.

rules.name: Objective (Accusative / Dative) Suffix '-no'
rules.description: Marks the direct object (especially when animate/definite) or indirect recipient: 'ang-no' (to me / me), 'bo-no' (to him / her), 'borok-no' (to the person).

rules.name: Genitive (Possessive) Suffix '-ni'
rules.description: Marks possession or origin: 'ang-ni' (my / mine), 'nwng-ni' (your / yours), 'bo-ni' (his / hers / its), 'Twipra-ni' (of Tripura).

rules.name: Locative Suffix '-o'
rules.description: Marks location in space or time ('in', 'at', 'on', 'to'): 'nok-o' (in the house / at home), 'kami-o' (in the village), 'dawk-o' (at the market), 'skul-o' (at school).

rules.name: Instrumental / Comitative Suffix '-bai'
rules.description: Means 'with' or 'by means of': 'ang-bai' (with me), 'ya-bai' (with hands), 'gari-bai' (by vehicle).

rules.name: Benefactive / Purposive Postposition '-bagwi'
rules.description: Means 'for' or 'for the sake of': 'ang-bagwi' (for me), 'nwng-bagwi' (for you), 'skul-bagwi' (for school).

authentic_examples.source: Pai (1976), Kokborok Grammar, CIIL, p. 30; Tripura Primers

source_references: Hoque, Faijul (2014), 'Kokborok: A Major Tribal Language of Tripura', IOSR-JHSS

sentence_construction.title: Basic Sentence Construction
sentence_construction.summary: Building authentic Kokborok sentences brings together SOV word order, numeral classifiers, case postpositions, and agglutinative verbal suffixes. By combining simple noun phrases with verbal predicates, learners can formulate daily conversational sentences.

rules.name: Step 1: Simple Equational Clauses (Nominal Predicates)
rules.description: In equational sentences ('A is B'), Kokborok does not require an overt copular verb ('to be') in simple present statements. The two noun phrases are juxtaposed directly.

examples.english: He/she is my friend. (Bo + angni yagwi, no overt copula needed)

rules.name: Step 2: Intransitive Action Sentences
rules.description: Structure: Subject (+ Locative/Adverb) + Intransitive Verb. For example: 'Ang' (I) + 'kamio' (to the village) + 'thangnai' (will go) = 'Ang kamio thangnai.'

examples.english: I will go to the village.

rules.name: Step 3: Transitive Action Sentences
rules.description: Structure: Subject + Object (+ Case) + Transitive Verb. For example: 'Ama' (Mother) + 'mai' (rice) + 'songo' (cooks) = 'Ama mai songo.'

rules.name: Step 4: Request & Question Formations
rules.description: To form a request, substitute the verb ending with '-di'. To form a polar question, append '-de'. For example: 'Nwng mai chakha' -> 'Nwng mai chakha de?' (Did you eat rice?).

authentic_examples.source: Tripura School Primers; Cultural Heritage Records

authentic_examples.english: I go to school and study.
Thank you very much, I am taking my leave.
authentic_examples.breakdown: Belaikheno hambai (Thank you very much), ang (I) thang-kha (leave-PAST/LEAVING)

source_references: Pai, Pushpa (1976), 'Kokborok Grammar', Central Institute of Indian Languages, pp. 80-94
Tripura Language Primers, Directorate of Kokborok & OML, Govt. of Tripura
